 This Petition, Coming On For Preliminary Hearing,
This Day, The Court Made The Following:
 Order

This writ petition is filed seeking for following reliefs:
(a) Issue a writ of certiorari or any other writ, to quash general award dated 28.12.2013, bearing no.KIADB/LAQ/1499/2013-14 passed by the 3rd respondent (Annexure-A) insofar it relates the land in Sy.no.262, measuring 3 acre 36 guntas situated at Kudumalakunte Village, Kasaba Hobli, Gowribidanur Taluk,
Chkkaballapur District.

(b) Issue a writ in the nature of mandamus or any other appropriate writ or direction,
directing the respondents no.2 and 3 to consider the case of the petitioners as per Section 29(2) of the KIADB Act for passing the consent award and issue a direction to the respondents no.2 and 3 to re-determine the compensation under Section 29(2) of the KIADB Act, within a reasonable period.

(c) Issue an writ in the nature of mandamus or any other appropriate writ or direction, directing the respondents no.2 and 3 to release 5/8th of the compensation amount within a reasonable period and etc.
2.

Sri Vijaya Kumar K., learned counsel for petitioners submitted that an extent of 3 acres 36 guntas in Sy.no.262 of Kudumalakunte Village, Kasaba Hobli, Gowribidanur Taluk, Chikkaballapura District was acquired by respondents for NC: 2023:KHC:39953 formation of Industrial Area.
It was submitted that father of petitioner namely Nyathonu @ Nyathappa S/o Doddaiah was owner of said land.

However, Smt.Aswathamma mother of respondents no.4 to 7 and respondents no.8 and 9 filed O.S.no.72/2011 against petitioners for relief of partition and separate possession in respect of land acquired claiming their 3/8th share.

In said suit, plaintiffs contended that Nyathappa had two wives Sri.K.N Nagaraju vs The State Of Karnataka on 8 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138219166/
3 namely Kotipi Lakshmamma and Lakshamma and they were children of Nyathappa through first wife.

sentences.text: 3. In said suit, petitioners entered appearance and filed written statement and contested matter and suit came to be dismissed on 07.06.2017.
Even R.A.no.21/2017 filed against it came to be dismissed on 31.05.2018.
It was submitted that though RSA.no.1555/2018 was filed and pending, there was no interim order in said appeal.

4. It was submitted that insofar as compensation amount in respect of acquired land, dispute between petitioners and respondents no.4 to 9, reference was made in LAC no.14/2014 for adjudication which was disposed of on 20.12.2019, holding that petitioners had established that they were legal representatives of deceased Nyathappa and entitled to receive compensation.

Insofar as claim of respondents no.4 NC: 2023:KHC:39953 to 9, Reference Court had observed that same was subject to establishing their rights in RSA.no.1555/2018.
5.
It was submitted that in view of said adjudication, petitioners submitted representation to respondents for payment of compensation under consent award.
It was further submitted that without providing opportunity to petitioners to avail compensation under consent award, General Award was passed and therefore seeks for quashing of same.

6. It was submitted that petitioners were in first instance claiming for passing of consent award only to extent of 5/8th share without giving up their right in respect of remaining, which would be subject to result of pending second appeal.
As such, there would be no impediment to respondents to pass consent award in respect of undisputed 5/8th share in favour of petitioners.
On above ground, sought for allowing writ petition.

7. On other hand, Sri P.V. Chandrashekar, learned counsel appearing for respondents no.2 and 3 submitted that since there was dispute with regard to title, respondents had proceeded to pass General Award.
Sri Manjunath V. Rayappa, learned Additional Government Advocate appearing for respondent no.1 sought to support said submission.

9. Heard learned counsel and perused writ petition record.
10.

From above submission and since dispute insofar as claim of respondents no.4 to 9 was adjudicated in LAC no.14/2014 and moreover when petitioners were claiming for consent award by keeping intact claim of respondents no.4 to 9 to be adjudicated in pending second appeal, there would be no justification for respondents to deny higher compensation to petitioners under consent award.

sentences.text: Accordingly, General Award at Annexure-A is quashed insofar as 3 acres 36 guntas in Sy.no.262 of Kudumalakunte Village, Kasaba Hobli, Gowribidanur Taluk, Chikkaballapura District.
Respondent no.3 shall pass consent award to extent of petitioners' share within three months from date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Needless to state that for said purposes, respondents would be entitled to secure any clarification or documents from petitioners.
Respondent no.3 would also be at liberty to withdraw proportionate compensation deposited before Reference Court.

Insofar as remaining extent, respondent no.3 to issue notice to petitioners as well as respondents no.4 to 9 and in case, they offer consent jointly, respondent no.3 to pass consent award in respect of said extent also and thereafter deposit said compensation before this Court in RSA.no.1555/2018,
which would remain subject to its final.
With above directions, writ petition is disposed of.
